record.question: Does cancelling the same original final after-session admission retain cleanup_unknown even when its original custody promise is settled synchronously by its own existing abort event, without waiting for a failure observer?

priorControlledEvidence.result: Two controlled schedules passed: both admitted -> clean, deliberately held sibling -> sticky UNKNOWN. The second did not prove behavior for cooperative cancellation.

sourceReasoning.finding: acquire sets pending=true, constructs tracked original beforeRequest promise, then calls boundV2Request immediately. beforeRequest is invoked from Promise.resolve().then, so the bounded abort subscription already exists before the controlled custody callback is entered.

pending is cleared only in the terminal then of that original work. Its abort catch emits typed ExecutionTransportFailure(cleanup_unknown,unknown) if pending remains true at that instant. It does not join the original admission before choosing that outcome.

beforeRequest reserves its request lease before awaiting native custody. On cancellation observed after the same custody returns, assertCurrent throws and the original catch releases that same lease synchronously before rejecting.

Final after-log and after-session are the only parallel reads; first rejection aborts their original cut. Typed cleanup_unknown is translated to native_read_cleanup_unknown and preferred when final results join. Later return does not replace that original result.

The same driver lifetime retains read-cut UNKNOWN and refuses confirmed dispose. Host close separately drains original request leases before the actual driver close, so an original driver-close first-failure is distinct from unresolved Host request drainage.
